questions.question: What is a service mesh?

options.text: A network topology for connecting microservices
A dedicated infrastructure layer for handling service-to-service communication in microservices
A hardware load balancer for container traffic

questions.explanation: Service mesh: infrastructure layer handling inter-service communication. Provides: traffic management, security (mTLS), observability—without changing application code. Examples: Istio, Linkerd, Consul Connect.

questions.question: What is a sidecar proxy in a service mesh?

options.text: A secondary proxy for failover scenarios
A proxy container deployed alongside each service instance that handles all network traffic
A backup service for disaster recovery

questions.explanation: Sidecar proxy: runs next to each service (same pod in Kubernetes). Intercepts all inbound/outbound traffic. Handles: load balancing, retries, circuit breaking, mTLS, metrics. Service unaware of mesh.

questions.question: What problems does a service mesh solve?
questions.explanation: Service mesh provides: security (automatic mTLS, authorization), traffic management (routing, load balancing, retries, circuit breaking), observability (metrics, distributed tracing). Cross-cutting concerns handled uniformly.

questions.question: What is the data plane in a service mesh?

options.text: The network layer handling data packet routing
The sidecar proxies that handle actual service traffic
A distributed database for service state

questions.explanation: Data plane: the sidecars (usually Envoy proxies). Handle actual traffic: routing, load balancing, health checks, metrics collection. Distributed across all service instances. Does the work.

questions.question: What is the control plane in a service mesh?

options.text: The centralized component that configures and manages the data plane proxies
The collection of sidecar proxies across all services

questions.explanation: Control plane: centralized management. Configures proxies, distributes policies, collects telemetry. Istio: istiod. Linkerd: control plane components. Provides API for operators to configure mesh behavior.

questions.question: What is Istio?

options.text: A popular open-source service mesh that uses Envoy proxies

questions.explanation: Istio: most popular service mesh. Uses Envoy sidecars. Features: traffic management, security policies, observability. Runs on Kubernetes. Powerful but complex. Backed by Google, IBM, Lyft.

questions.question: What is mTLS (mutual TLS) in a service mesh?

options.text: Both client and server authenticate each other with certificates, encrypting all service-to-service traffic

questions.explanation: mTLS: mutual authentication. Both sides present certificates. Service mesh automates: certificate generation, rotation, verification. All traffic encrypted. Zero-trust networking without code changes.

questions.question: What is the overhead of using a service mesh?

options.text: Latency (extra network hop through proxy), resource usage (sidecar per service), complexity

questions.explanation: Service mesh overhead: latency (typically 1-3ms per hop), memory/CPU for sidecars, operational complexity. At scale, sidecar resources add up. Evaluate if benefits outweigh costs for your use case.

questions.question: When should you NOT use a service mesh?

options.text: Simple applications with few services, or when the overhead isn't justified

questions.explanation: Skip service mesh for: monoliths, few services (overhead not worth it), simple networking needs, resource-constrained environments. Service mesh shines at scale with complex networking requirements.

questions.question: What is Envoy proxy?

options.text: A reverse proxy for API gateway implementations
A high-performance proxy used as the data plane in many service meshes
A distributed database proxy for connection pooling
A programming framework for building proxies

questions.explanation: Envoy: L7 proxy originally from Lyft. Features: dynamic configuration, extensive observability, extensible. Used by: Istio, AWS App Mesh, Consul Connect. De facto standard for service mesh data planes.

questions.question: What is traffic shifting in a service mesh?

options.text: Gradually routing traffic between service versions for canary deployments or A/B testing

questions.explanation: Traffic shifting: route percentages to different versions. Canary: 5% to v2, 95% to v1. Gradually increase. A/B testing: route by headers. Blue-green: instant switch. Service mesh makes this declarative.

questions.question: A company has 200 microservices and needs consistent security, observability, and traffic management. Best approach?

options.text: Deploy a service mesh to handle cross-cutting concerns uniformly

questions.explanation: 200 services: implementing security/observability in each is inconsistent and expensive. Service mesh: uniform mTLS, metrics, tracing across all services. One place to configure policies. Worth the overhead at this scale.
